- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots in next 3–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8%.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3 days, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 10–15 day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply linear decay correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day after day 7.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive negative values, model underestimates; apply upward bias of 3–6% for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.3) and price is trending, model often misses momentum; add 1–2% upward bias if price > 10% above 14-day MA.
